runbooks.title: SOP-PW-101: Primary Transfer Pump Trip or Mechanical Failure
steps: 1. Confirm zero discharge flow and loss of discharge pressure (<15 psi) on primary transfer pump P-1.
2. Verify standby transfer pump P-2 status is STANDBY / HEALTHY and isolation valves are open.
3. Check gathering tank fill level and verify decision deadline before tank high-high threshold is reached.
4. If decision deadline allows, execute start sequence for standby pump P-2 via control console.
5. If standby pump P-2 is unavailable or fails to start, immediately initiate value-ranked well curtailment (SOP-PW-204).
6. Dispatch field technician to inspect P-1 local disconnect, motor bearings, and seal flush.
safety_warnings: DO NOT attempt to restart tripped pump without visual local inspection if breaker tripped on overcurrent.
Ensure pipeline header pressure is below 110 psi before bringing standby pump on line.

runbooks.title: SOP-PW-204: Value-Ranked Wellhead Water Curtailment Protocol
steps: 1. Identify active producing wells routed to Gathering Tank A.
2. Query economic ranking for wells ordered by lowest oil margin per barrel of produced water.
3. Curtail Avon 12-H (W-12, margin $5.40/bbl water) by 80% to achieve immediate 44 bbl/h reduction.
4. If additional buffer is required, curtail Avon 7-H (W-7, margin $8.20/bbl water) to achieve 36 bbl/h reduction.
5. Preserve high-oil producer Avon 1-H (W-1, margin $32.50/bbl water) online unless total station shutdown is mandatory.
6. Notify production foreman and record deferred production barrels in shift handoff.
safety_warnings: Choke adjustments must be executed gradually over 15-20 minutes to prevent sand bridging at wellhead.

runbooks.title: SOP-PW-305: Ultrasonic Sensor Verification & Manual Gauge Tape
steps: 1. Check 3-way sensor trust panel. Identify whether ultrasonic, optical camera, or mass-balance is the outlier.
2. If chemical defoamer was recently dosed or surface turbulence is high, ultrasonic transducer may read false echo.
3. Dispatch field technician with calibrated innage tape to manually dip Tank A through thief hatch.
4. Compare manual tape reading against SCADA ultrasonic reading.
5. If manual dip confirms camera and mass-balance reading, flag ultrasonic gauge as faulty and widen forecast uncertainty band.
safety_warnings: Thief hatch dipping requires grounding cable attachment and H2S personal monitor worn on breathing zone.

runbooks.title: SOP-PW-402: Emergency Pipeline Interconnect & Water Trucking
steps: 1. Review commercial disposal interconnect line capacity (max 80 bbl/h).
2. Verify contract tariff rate ($1.20/bbl) and notify pipeline controller.
3. Open automated motorized valve MOV-201 to divert water to alternate line.
4. If trucking is required, note that truck dispatch carries 60-minute mobilization lead time.
5. Water haul trucks must only be ordered if time to high-high threshold exceeds 60 minutes.
safety_warnings: Verify receiving facility tank ullage before opening interconnect valve.

historical_incidents.summary: Transfer Pump P-1 VFD failure during night shift
historical_incidents.root_cause: VFD cooling fan failure caused drive thermal overload trip on P-1.
historical_incidents.action_taken: Operator approved starting standby pump P-2 at 03:22 (7 min after trip). Outflow restored to 120 bbl/h. Curtailment avoided.
historical_incidents.outcome: Successful recovery. Tank level peaked at 520 bbl (well below 800 bbl threshold). Total response cost $250.
historical_incidents.lessons_learned: Quick decision to switch to standby pump within 10 minutes saved ~$12,500/hr forced shutdown cost.

historical_incidents.summary: Water-cut surge from Avon 7-H following frac hit
historical_incidents.root_cause: Offset operator completed stage causing immediate water-cut jump from 45 bbl/h to 110 bbl/h.
historical_incidents.action_taken: Rerouted 70 bbl/h to Tank B buffer while well W-12 was curtailed by 80%.
historical_incidents.outcome: Station remained balanced without spilling or trucking. Total cost $668.
historical_incidents.lessons_learned: Value-ranked curtailment of low-margin well W-12 mitigated surge without shutting down high-margin well W-1.

historical_incidents.summary: Ultrasonic gauge false high level reading from defoamer foam
historical_incidents.root_cause: Overdosing of defoamer surfactant created a 14-inch dense foam layer causing ultrasonic false echo at 72%.
historical_incidents.action_taken: Console highlighted sensor disagreement and widened P10-P90 band. Field tech dipped tank with gauge tape and confirmed 41.5%. No shutdown needed.
historical_incidents.outcome: Prevented false emergency shutdown. Saved estimated $20,500 in unnecessary shutdown and truck callout fees.
historical_incidents.lessons_learned: Trust arbitration between camera and flow balance successfully prevented an unnecessary operator panic shutdown.
